subject: Re: Unexpected October overrun — temporary reconciliation & escrow offer
body:
From: Julian Moore <julian.moore@helixai.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Helix AI Billing <billing@helixai.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected October overrun — urgent reconciliation help requested

Sofia,

We just pulled October invoices and saw a ~42% overrun compared to our committed baseline (see attached usage_report_Oct2026.csv). That spike came from a short series of A/B experiments during our product launch (11/1–11/3 window) but the scale exceeded our burst buffer.

We need a path to reconcile the overage and avoid surprise cashflow pressure for our finance team. Specifically:
- Is there any one-time credit or smoothing you can apply while we sort internal controls?
- Can we put a temporary headroom in place for the week of Nov 8 to avoid a repeat?
- If an escrow/advance deposit helps lower the effective overage rate, can you outline terms?

Appreciate quick confirmation and a contact for the billing/legal lead if we need a DocuSign.

Thanks,
Julian
Julian Moore
Head of Platform, Helix AI
julian.moore@helixai.com

----------------------------------------------------------------

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Julian Moore <julian.moore@helixai.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected October overrun — urgent reconciliation help requested

Julian — thanks for the note and the report. Im sorry you ran into that during launch week. We can absolutely work through a short-term reconciliation so this doesnt create a cashflow hit.

Quick plan from our side:
1) Temporary headroom: we can open a controlled cap for Nov 8–14 with a rate uplift rather than charging full overrun at list. That should prevent throttles while you lock down experiment limits.
2) One-time smoothing: Jordan will propose a blended true-up for the Oct overrun that amortizes the excess across Nov/Dec invoices.
3) Escrow option: finance has an option where Helix posts an escrow deposit that buys you a lower marginal rate on burst usage; markus_klein is looped for terms.

Im looping Jordan (account lead) and Marissa (strategic credits) to put numbers to these options. If youd like, we can schedule a 30-min call today to go over numbers and get a DocuSign ready.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Sales Manager — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

----------------------------------------------------------------

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Julian Moore <julian.moore@helixai.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 10:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected October overrun — urgent reconciliation help requested

Julian — quick numbers here based on the usage file. Two options that are commonly used and we can finalize whichever you prefer:

Option A — Amortized True-up:
- Apply a promotional smoothing credit equivalent to 25% of the overrun this cycle, with the remaining 75% spread evenly over Nov and Dec invoices.
- No upfront deposit required.
- This preserves your committed tier for future months.

Option B — Escrow-backed Burst Discount:
- Helix posts a refundable escrow deposit equal to 30% of projected monthly burst (we can estimate from the attached CSV).
- In exchange: a 40% discount on marginal overrun rates while escrow is held; escrow refundable after a 90-day audit window with any adjustments applied.
- We can draft a short DocuSign for this.

If neither fits, tell us your target (e.g., % of overrun to credit) and well work to match. I can also lock a 1-week temporary headroom (Nov 8–14) with a soft-rate cap so you dont get throttled.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
jordan_blake@redwood.com

----------------------------------------------------------------

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Julian Moore <julian.moore@helixai.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected October overrun — urgent reconciliation help requested

Julian — adding context from a credit perspective. Given Helixs multi-quarter commit and usage history, we can offer the following blended package as an exception:

- Immediate one-time credit equal to 20% of the documented overrun amount.
- Remaining overrun balance amortized 50/50 over November and December invoices.
- If Helix chooses the escrow option (Option B), well increase the marginal overrun discount to 45% instead of 40% and apply the 20% one-time credit as well.
- We need an acceptance email from Helix and a signed short-form escrow agreement to execute. Ive attached a proposed_escrow_agreement.pdf (stub).

Happy to get this executed today if you confirm.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Director, North America
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed_escrow_agreement.pdf (PDF, 78 KB)

----------------------------------------------------------------

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected October overrun — urgent reconciliation help requested

All — finance sign-off on the package below with one note on timing:

- Approved: 20% one-time credit + amortization plan (50/50 over Nov/Dec) OR escrow-backed variant with enhanced marginal discount.
- Escrow mechanics: refundable deposit held in third-party escrow; deposit reconciled after 90 days with offsets for any sustained over-usage beyond the agreed window.
- We will not net against other invoices; credit will appear as a line item \"Promotional True-up Credit (Oct 2026)\" on the next invoice.

If Helix elects escrow, legal will need the signed short-form agreement (Marissa, please route).

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Finance — Contracts & Billing
markus_klein@redwood.com

----------------------------------------------------------------

From: Julian Moore <julian.moore@helixai.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected October overrun — urgent reconciliation help requested

Team — thanks for the quick response and for spelling out the options. Well take Option B (escrow-backed) to smooth our cashflow and get the enhanced marginal discount. Action items on our side:

- Ill route the short-form escrow to our legal and billing teams today. Please send the DocuSign link and the final escrow amount calculation based on the attached usage CSV.
- Well provide the deposit within 3 business days of sign-off.
- Please confirm the Nov 8–14 temporary headroom is in place once the DocuSign is sent.

Appreciate the responsiveness — Julian

Julian Moore
Head of Platform, Helix AI
julian.moore@helixai.com

Attachments referenced: usage_report_Oct2026.csv (CSV, 42 KB); proposed_escrow_agreement.pdf (PDF, 78 KB)
